hook.text: A surgery with a 90% survival rate sounds safe. A surgery with a 10% death rate sounds dangerous. Same operation.

buildup.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that framing changes decisions. Positive frames promote risk-taking.

discovery.text: In the Asian Disease Problem, people chose the safe option when framed as lives saved and the risky one when framed as.

twist.text: Framing is everywhere. 80% lean beef sells better than 20% fat beef. Same meat. The frame changes perceived quality.

climax.text: Rational choice theory says framing should not matter. But it always does. How you say it changes what people choose.

punchline.text: 90% survival or 10% death. Same fact. Different frame changes the choice.

quiz.question: What is the framing effect?
options: How information is presented changes decisions even when the underlying facts are identical
